# CRW-895 after the second verification of ad1b3d605: the find placeholder inside the text of a shell, POSIX character classes in a
# find name pattern, and a filter that reads a file instead of standard input. ../repo is the managed checkout itself.

=== CRW-895-n1 | R
--why find substitutes {} in the text of a shell too; the body removes the checkout through git.
find ../repo -exec sh -c 'git worktree remove --force {}' \;

=== CRW-895-n2 | R
--why The body removes the slot root's content: .. is an ancestor of the checkout.
find .. -exec bash -c 'rm -rf {}' \;

=== CRW-895-n3 | R
--why rmdir in the body takes the substituted start point.
find ../repo -exec sh -c 'rmdir {}' \;

=== CRW-895-n4 | R
--why -execdir and a quoted placeholder in a longer word are substituted as well.
find ../repo -execdir sh -c 'rm -rf "x/{}"' \;

=== CRW-895-n5 | B
--why A start inside the checkout, with the placeholder in the body.
find build -exec sh -c 'rm -rf {}' \;

=== CRW-895-n6 | B
--why A test before the action keeps the checkout itself out, whatever the body does with the placeholder.
find . -name '*.o' -exec sh -c 'rm -f {}' \;

=== CRW-895-n7 | R
--why A start at the checkout with no test, the placeholder in the body.
find . -exec sh -c 'rm -rf {}' \;

=== CRW-895-n8 | R
--why The shell's positional parameter is the placeholder.
find ../repo -exec sh -c 'rm -rf "$1"' _ {} \;

=== CRW-895-n9 | B
--why The body ignores the placeholder and the start is the checkout: a fixed removal inside it.
find ../repo -exec sh -c 'rm build/old.o' \;

=== CRW-895-o1 | R
--why [[:alpha:]]* fits repo; a POSIX class does not end the bracket at its first ].
find ../repo -name '[[:alpha:]]*' -delete

=== CRW-895-o2 | R
--why [[:print:]]* fits repo as well.
find ../repo -name '[[:print:]]*' -delete

=== CRW-895-o3 | B
--why [[:digit:]]* does not fit repo, so the test leaves the checkout out.
find ../repo -name '[[:digit:]]*' -delete

=== CRW-895-o4 | R
--why A class inside a longer bracket still fits r.
find ../repo -name '[[:digit:]r]*' -delete

=== CRW-895-o5 | B
--why A negated class that excludes the first letter of repo.
find ../repo -name '[^[:alpha:]]*' -delete

=== CRW-895-q1 | R
--why cat reads the file operand, not the standard input that holds the name; the list it prints is not the producer's.
echo ../other | cat roots.list | xargs git worktree remove --force

=== CRW-895-q2 | R
--why sort and head read a file operand too.
echo build | sort roots.list | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-q3 | R
--why grep's operands after the pattern are files.
echo ../other | grep o roots.list | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-q4 | B
--why cat - reads standard input; the name is inside the checkout.
echo build/old.o | cat - | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-q5 | B
--why grep with the pattern only reads standard input.
echo build/old.o | grep old | xargs rm
